query: Refractory high-entropy alloys are promising structural materials, but achieving a strong combination of strength and plasticity remains important. What single intervention could improve this strength–plasticity combination? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate reference alloy, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled, small fraction of Ti to a baseline NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy will improve the strength–plasticity combination by enhancing grain boundary cohesion.
generation.material_initial_state: A NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy exhibiting a mainly BCC structure with high strength but limited room-temperature plasticity.
generation.intervention: Microalloying by introducing a small amount of Titanium (Ti) into the NbMoTaW alloy composition, processed via established routes.
generation.conditions: The alloy is processed under identical conditions (e.g., mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering) and tested at room temperature (and potentially elevated temperatures) under compressive/tensile regimes, with the only change being the Ti addition.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced grain boundary cohesion and potentially a slightly refined microstructure due to Ti segregation at the grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Ti atoms preferentially segregate to grain boundaries, reducing inherent grain boundary weaknesses. This increased cohesion mitigates premature intergranular fracture and allows for greater plastic deformation without compromising the high intrinsic strength of the BCC matrix.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline NbMoTaW alloy, the Ti-added alloy is expected to exhibit improved ductility while maintaining or even slightly improving yield strength.
generation.baseline: The NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy without any Ti addition.
generation.boundary: This improvement is anticipated when the alloy is processed by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering under controlled atmospheres, with testing performed at room temperature (and/or elevated temperatures) as per standardized mechanical tests.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the enhancement in ductility and any strength change depends on the precise Ti concentration and processing parameters; thus, while the qualitative improvement is expected, quantitative gains remain to be optimized.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy samples using identical processing parameters (e.g., mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering): one set as the control (no Ti) and the other with a defined small Ti addition (e.g., around 5 at.%). Subject both sets to standardized tensile and/or compression tests to measure yield strength and ductility.
measurements: Quantitative assessment of yield strength via stress–strain curves
Microstructural analysis (e.g., TEM/SEM) for grain boundary characteristics and Ti segregation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ti-added samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in ductility without a detrimental reduction in yield strength (compared to the control under identical testing conditions), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: One of the most promising and progressive fields in modern material science is high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The first to propose HEAs’ concept was J.W. Yeh [], but since then, it has changed rather significantly, especially during the last few years []. Due to their extremely high mechanical and physical properties, refractory HEAs are classified as a separate group of materials. Such alloying compositions mainly include elements from the IV, V, and VI columns of the periodic table with some additions of Al, Si, Ni, or Co []. First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [,]. It was found that the alloys possess higher mechanical properties at higher temperatures in comparison to conventional superalloys, such as Inconel 718 and Haynes 230 []. It was also determined that the addition of V increases the hardness significantly (up to 11.4 GPa at 1150 °C) [] and yield strength σ0.2 from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa [].
